problem: The geometric series $5+15+⋯+405$ can be expressed using sigma notation as
worked_solution:
We must express the given series in the form

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ denotes the first term of the series, $r$ denotes the common ratio, and $N$ denotes the number of terms in the series. In this case, ${a}_{1}=5.$

To find $r,$ we find the ratio of the consecutive terms ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{15}{5}=3
$$

Now we must determine $N$ (the index of the last term). To do this, we use the fact that

$$
{a}_{N}={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{N-1}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{N-1} \\ 405 & =5\cdot {3}^{N-1} \\ 81 & ={3}^{N-1} \\ {3}^{4} & ={3}^{N-1} \\ 4 & =N-1 \\ N & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing the geometric series in sigma notation, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}5+15+⋯+405 & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{5}5\cdot {3}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$
